title: Annotation-based learner's personality modeling in distance learning context
reason: Annotation traces in an online reading environment are related to Big Five traits (meets I2/I4 in substance), but both samples are adult volunteers of mixed occupations, mostly academics with professorship degrees, not higher-education students.

extraction.country: Tunisia (author affiliations; study site not stated)
extraction.design: correlational + multiple regression; validation against NEO-IPIP
extraction.n_quote: We recruited 100 volunteers (35 women and 65 men) aged between 22 and 50 years. Most of the participants have the professorship degree in scientific or literary disciplines.
extraction.population: adult volunteers aged 22-50, mostly academics/graduates (validation study); prior study 120 volunteers 'with different occupations and interests'
extraction.lms_indicators: annotation-act counts in the i-Read online reading environment (total, average, graphical, textual, reference, compound annotations)

effect_sizes.between: number of textual annotation acts (NTAA) ↔ conscientiousness
total number of annotation acts (TNAA) ↔ neuroticism
average number of annotation acts (ANAA) ↔ extraversion

effect_sizes.quote: prediction regarding Conscientiousness is reasonably accurate, with R2 value of 0.12
For Neuroticism we obtained the model with the best fit, with an R2 value of 0.14

extraction.notes: Table 1 cells verified against the PDF page image. Table 1 and 2 reproduce the authors' prior study (Omheni et al., 2014; 120 volunteers) - secondary E2 for those numbers; the new validation (n = 100) reports only p-values and RMSE (Tables 4-5). Borderline: if the adjudicator accepts academic/graduate volunteers as an HE sample, the record would meet I2/I4.
